text: By the book's rule for negating quantified statements, ¬(∀x P(x)) is equivalent to:
explanation: The book gives ¬(∀x P(x)) ≡ ∃x ¬P(x): swap ∀ to ∃ and negate the predicate, producing a counterexample. The book explicitly flags ∀x ¬P(x) ('for none') as the classic 'not all means none' error; ∃x P(x) forgets to negate the predicate; and ¬∃x ¬P(x) is equivalent to the original ∀x P(x).
